title: Fine-Tuning Qwen3-8B with Tinker: From 50% to 76% Accuracy, and Burning Through My Budget
why_read: A hands-on walkthrough of fine-tuning a small open-weight model to triage prompt complexity, a practical and relatable cost-optimization pattern for LLM apps.
analysis: The author fine-tunes Qwen3-8B using a service called Tinker to build a 'Complexity Scorer' that routes simple prompts to cheaper models and complex ones to expensive reasoning models, reporting an accuracy jump from 50% to 76%. This is a commonly useful pattern in production LLM systems, often called model routing or cascading, and seeing a concrete fine-tuning walkthrough with real numbers is useful even if informal. It's a hackathon submission so the rigor is limited, and the 'burning through budget' framing suggests practical lessons about fine-tuning costs that other engineers will relate to. Overall a decent practical case study rather than a polished research contribution.
